episodes.name: Era Kovanxhi
post: I recently had the pleasure of interviewing the CEO of BonDo soup, Ms. Era Kovanxhi. Over the past two years I have worked with Ms. Era on executive function skills research at Cedar Hill Preparatory School. A few months ago, when I mentioned my interest in biotechnology and food science, she introduced me to the klotho protein which she has done deep research on in the past. In this episode, Ms. Era describes how she came upon the klotho protein, a natural body chemical that aids in cell health and controls aging, and is working on a product that aids in the production of this protein for those on the go, elderly, and people affected by illness. Through her extensive research and own experience as a busy college student and individual in the workforce, she needed something quick and easy that could provide her with the nutrients she needed. This is how BonDo soup was born. Through talking to founders, I have realized that many of the best products come out of necessity. She has created nutrient dense soup bits created from healthy, whole, and all natural ingredients that she found in her kitchen.

This fall, I will be working with Ms. Era to conduct research on her soup bits and their relation to klotho production in a two part study. In the fall, we will be conducting wet lab research to measure our findings. Additionally, in the spring, we will be asking for consumer feedback on the product to see how customers respond.

It has been such a pleasure learning from Ms. Era through this process. Hearing about her experience as a founder in the food product development space and my involvement in her product's research and testing serve to help me grow as a learner and someone curious about the food industry. Being at the forefront of the process allows me to learn about food development and the founder mentality firsthand.

Your favorite foodie signing off,
Samyuktha
